description: Renovate covers the Ansible layers only. Terraform and GitHub Actions stay with Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml), which already works and matches the repo's SHA-plus-semver-comment pinning convention. Two bots is mild noise; migrating two working ecosystems is a separate project.
enabledManagers is an allowlist, so a manager added upstream cannot start opening PRs against terraform/ or .github/workflows/ on its own.

pip_requirements.description: constraints.txt is not matched by default; it is the ansible-core pin.

customManagers.description: Activates the '# renovate: datasource=... depName=...' comments already present in role defaults (rustfs_version, rustfs_boto3_version, rustfs_botocore_version). They predate this config and nothing was acting on them.

packageRules.description: The collection closure is exact-pinned, so one collection moving can violate a sibling's floor or push ansible-core outside a requires_ansible ceiling. A grouped PR is the smallest unit that can be judged coherent, and `make validate-collections` gates it. Per-collection PRs would each pass lint while leaving the closure inconsistent.

The system under test. Excluded because the pin exists for benchmark reproducibility and must only move via a deliberate, hand-authored PR. Matched by URL fragment as well as FQCN: the entry is a git source, and Renovate derives the depName from the repository URL rather than from the Galaxy name (renovatebot/renovate discussion #27022). Both forms are listed because the derived value is unverified until a dry run confirms it -- see task 6.5.
boto3 and botocore move together or the SDK is half-pinned; group them so a mismatched pair cannot be merged one PR at a time.
packageRules.groupName: aws sdk for the rustfs role

packageRules.description: ansible-core moves only with a re-checked requires_ansible intersection; never unattended.
